pharm: An imidazoquinoline applied to the skin that activates Toll-like receptor 7 on dendritic cells and macrophages, triggering local release of interferon-alpha, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and other cytokines. This stimulates an innate and cell-mediated immune response that clears virally infected and dysplastic/neoplastic keratinocytes. Systemic absorption through intact skin is minimal.
quick: 5% cream applied topically at bedtime; schedule varies by indication (2x, 3x, or 5x/week)
Available human data have not identified a drug-associated risk; minimal systemic absorption
Low systemic levels; use with caution, avoid infant contact with treated skin
No adjustment - negligible systemic absorption through intact skin
Local skin reactions (erythema, erosion, scabbing) and flu-like systemic symptoms
summary: Imiquimod 5% cream is a topical immune-response modifier that activates Toll-like receptor 7, inducing local interferon and other cytokines to clear abnormal or virally infected keratinocytes. It is FDA-approved for clinically typical, nonhyperkeratotic actinic keratoses of the face and scalp, biopsy-confirmed superficial basal cell carcinoma when surgery is unsuitable, and external genital and perianal warts (condylomata acuminata). It is applied at bedtime, left on for 6-10 hours, then washed off; the dosing frequency and duration depend on the indication. Expected and clinically meaningful local skin reactions - erythema, flaking, erosion, scabbing, and weeping - signal the immune response but can be intense enough to require a rest period. Flu-like systemic symptoms (fatigue, fever, myalgia, headache) may occur. Because systemic absorption through intact skin is minimal, renal, hepatic, pregnancy, and lactation considerations are limited.
indications: Actinic keratosis - clinically typical, nonhyperkeratotic, nonhypertrophic lesions on the face or scalp in immunocompetent adults

Superficial basal cell carcinoma - biopsy-confirmed primary lesions up to 2.0 cm on the trunk (excluding anogenital skin), neck, or extremities (excluding hands/feet), when surgical methods are medically less appropriate and follow-up can be assured
External genital and perianal warts / condylomata acuminata in patients 12 years and older

dosage.d: Apply once daily at bedtime 2 times per week (e.g., Mon/Thu) for a full 16 weeks, to a contiguous treatment area up to ~25 cm2 on face or scalp
dosage.n: Use up to one packet per application; leave on ~8 hours then wash off

dosage.d: Apply once daily at bedtime 5 times per week for a full 6 weeks; apply enough to cover the tumor plus 1 cm of surrounding skin (about 10 mg for 0.5-1.0 cm, 25 mg for 1.0-1.5 cm, 40 mg for 1.5-2.0 cm tumors)
dosage.n: Leave on ~8 hours then wash off; confirm clearance clinically/by biopsy at follow-up

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer once daily at bedtime 3 times per week until total wart clearance or for a maximum of 16 weeks
dosage.n: Leave on 6-10 hours then wash off; ages 12+; rub in until no longer visible

admin: Apply at bedtime to clean, dry skin; rub in until the cream is no longer visible
Wash hands before and after applying; do not apply to broken skin, internally, or to the eyes, lips, or nostrils
Leave on for the indicated time (about 8 hours for AK/sBCC, 6-10 hours for warts), then wash the area with mild soap and water
Use unit-dose packets; discard any partially used packet - do not reuse
Avoid occlusive dressings; do not apply more frequently or for longer than prescribed (increases reaction severity)
A rest period of several days may be taken if local skin reactions become too intense, then resume
Avoid sexual contact while the cream is on the skin (genital warts); it may weaken condoms and diaphragms
moa: Imiquimod is an imidazoquinoline immune-response modifier that acts as an agonist at Toll-like receptor 7 (and to a lesser degree TLR8) on dendritic cells, monocytes/macrophages, and keratinocytes. Receptor activation induces nuclear factor-kappa-B signaling and the local production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, chiefly interferon-alpha, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6, and IL-12. These cytokines stimulate the innate immune system and promote a Th1-skewed, cell-mediated immune response that recruits and activates cytotoxic effector cells against human papillomavirus-infected, actinically damaged, and neoplastic keratinocytes. The precise mechanism by which it clears AK, sBCC, and external genital warts is not fully established, but immune-mediated lesion destruction is the prevailing explanation.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to imiquimod or any component of the cream is a practical contraindication
relative: Use on skin not yet healed from prior drug or surgical treatment
Autoimmune disease or immunosuppression (response and safety less predictable)
Sunburned, irritated, or inflamed treatment skin (defer until resolved)
monitor: Severity of local skin reactions (erythema, erosion, weeping, scabbing)
Localized hypopigmentation/depigmentation, which can be permanent
Signs of secondary infection of treated skin

preg: Available data from case reports and case series with imiquimod use in pregnant women have not identified a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, and systemic absorption through intact skin is minimal. Animal studies at exposures far above the maximum recommended human dose showed no adverse developmental effects at non-maternally-toxic doses. There are no adequate and well-controlled trials; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Systemic concentrations of imiquimod after topical application are low, so the amount in human milk is expected to be minimal. It may be used with caution during breastfeeding; avoid applying to the chest/breast area and prevent the infant from coming into contact with treated skin or the cream (mouth/eyes).
renal: No dose adjustment is required. Because absorption through intact skin is negligible, renal impairment is not expected to affect systemic exposure; formal studies in renal impairment have not been performed.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required. Minimal systemic absorption means hepatic impairment is not expected to meaningfully alter exposure; formal studies in hepatic impairment have not been performed.

moderate: Concomitant use with any other imiquimod-containing product on the same area increases the severity of local skin reactions - avoid
minor: No clinically significant systemic drug-drug interactions have been identified given minimal absorption

serious: Intense local inflammatory reaction with weeping/erosion requiring interruption
Severe vulvar swelling leading to urinary retention
rare: Systemic flu-like illness with chills and myalgia
emergency: Urinary retention from severe genital swelling
Severe systemic flu-like reaction with high fever

monitoring: Local skin reactions - erythema, erosion, scabbing, weeping - and need for a rest period
Systemic flu-like symptoms (fever, fatigue, myalgia, headache)
Clearance response of lesions; for sBCC confirm cure clinically and consider biopsy at follow-up
Signs of secondary bacterial infection of treated skin
counsel: Apply a thin layer at bedtime exactly as scheduled - more is not better and increases skin reactions
Wash your hands before and after, leave the cream on for the time your doctor specified, then wash the area with mild soap and water
Expect redness, flaking, scabbing, and sometimes raw or weeping skin - this is the medicine working; if it becomes too painful, you may pause for a few days
You may feel flu-like (tired, achy, mild fever) - tell your doctor if this is severe
Protect treated skin from sun and sunlamps; use sunscreen and protective clothing
For genital warts: avoid sex while the cream is on, and note it can weaken condoms and diaphragms; this clears visible warts but does not cure the underlying virus
Skin color changes at the site can be permanent; report lasting lightening of the skin
pk: Local immune/inflammatory response develops over days of repeated application
Clinical lesion clearance over weeks of the full treatment course
Apparent terminal half-life ~20-30 hours after topical dosing (minimal absorption)
Sustained local cytokine response; benefit assessed at end of the prescribed course
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); avoid freezing; single-use packets, discard after use
pearls: Robust local skin reaction (erythema, erosion, scabbing) is expected and correlates with response - reassure patients rather than stopping prematurely
Dosing differs by indication: AK 2x/week x16 wk, sBCC 5x/week x6 wk, external warts 3x/week up to 16 wk
Use only on biopsy-confirmed superficial BCC when surgery is less appropriate, and ensure reliable follow-up
Clears visible genital warts but does not eradicate HPV; recurrence is common - counsel accordingly
May weaken latex condoms and diaphragms - advise alternative contraception during use for genital warts
Hypopigmentation/depigmentation at the site can be permanent; flu-like systemic symptoms may occur
missed: If you miss an application, apply it as soon as you remember that night, then continue your regular schedule; do not apply extra cream to make up a missed dose, as this increases skin reactions. If it is already near morning, skip it and resume at the next scheduled bedtime.
overdose: Topical over-application increases the risk of severe local skin reactions and may raise the chance of systemic reactions. Accidental ingestion of 200 mg or more (equivalent to about 16 packets) has been associated with hypotension that resolved with oral or intravenous fluids. Management is symptomatic and supportive; contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the US).
